title: Jadotville: The Company That Surrendered but Was Never Beaten
summary: Recounts how, in September nineteen sixty-one, in the breakaway Congolese province of Katanga, the hundred-and-fifty-five-man Irish A Company, sent to the town of Jadotville on behalf of the United Nations peacekeeping force, held out for five days against thousands of Katangese gendarmes led by European mercenaries. The episode ranges from the trenches Commandant Pat Quinlan had his men dig to the relief column halted at the Lufira Bridge, from a company out of water and ammunition surrendering without a single death to the soldiers branded cowards in their own country for decades after returning from captivity, and to the recognition that came late.
